contracts.statement: A todo is the JSON object { id: number, text: string, done: boolean }. Ids start at 1 and are assigned as Math.max(0, ...existing ids) + 1, so an id is never reused after a remove. This shape is the on-disk format of ~/.todos.json and must match exactly across src/todo.js, src/cli.js, test/todo.test.js and test/cli.test.js.

src/cli.js exports exactly one function, run(argv, io), where argv is the array of arguments after the program name (process.argv.slice(2)) and io is { homeDir: string, write: (line: string) => void }. run returns a number exit code (0 on success, 1 on a usage or lookup error) and never calls process.exit. src/todo.js exports STORAGE_FILE = '.todos.json', CHECK_MARK = '✓' (U+2713), todosPath(homeDir), loadTodos(homeDir), saveTodos(homeDir, todos), addTodo(homeDir, text), completeTodo(homeDir, id), removeTodo(homeDir, id) and formatTodos(todos, pendingOnly); every function that touches disk takes homeDir as its first argument, and completeTodo/removeTodo return null when no todo matches the id. os.homedir() is referenced only in bin/todo.js.

formatTodos(todos, pendingOnly) returns one line per todo shaped as `${id}. ${done ? '✓ ' : ''}${text}`, joined with a single newline, and returns the empty string when there is nothing to show (empty list, or pendingOnly with no pending todos). A done line therefore reads '1. ✓ buy milk' and a pending line reads '1. buy milk'. Tests assert against formatTodos output and the CLI prints that string through io.write, so src/todo.js, src/cli.js and both test files must agree on this exact spacing and on the check mark being U+2713.
